entries.text: **Importance That Changes Book to Book** - One of Penpoint's most-requested features since Series arrived. A character who carries your first book can fade into the background by the third, and their Importance can now say so: set it per book while viewing "This Book," and "All Books" shows you the whole picture at a glance. Items and locations work the same way, and standalone books are unchanged.

**A Second Way to Read a Chapter: By Scene** - The Chapters page has always grouped a chapter's content by block, description, cast, and so on, all at once across the whole chapter. A new View Mode button flips you to By Scene instead, stacking each scene in turn with your layout repeated inside it, so the chapter reads as a scene-by-scene outline. Penpoint remembers your choice, and By Group stays the default.

**Placeholder Cards Inside Folders** - Placeholders can now live inside a chapter group, even one that holds no chapters yet, so you can rough out a whole section as a stack of cards before a word of it is written. Promoting one now creates the chapter right inside that folder.

**Corkboard Card Size** - The Corkboard's cog menu now lets you pick how big your index cards are: Compact fits more of your book on screen at once, Large gives you room to read your summaries, and Standard is what you've been using. Compact drops the subtitle and first line of prose to save space; switch to a bigger card to see them again.

**Merging Scenes Now Asks First** - Pressing Backspace at the start of a scene (or Delete at the end of the one above) used to join the two scenes instantly, with nothing on screen to say it had happened. Penpoint now asks first, naming both scenes and what becomes of them. Tick "Don't ask again" if you do this on purpose; the switch to bring the prompt back lives in manuscript settings.

**Profile Pictures Show Up in More Places** - Wherever a character, item, or location appears in a list, its profile picture now shows instead of a plain icon: character sheet blocks, chapter cast and setting lists, item and location pages, the Minipen sidebar, and search results. Anything without a picture keeps its familiar icon.

**Colored Highlighting Everywhere** - The colored highlighter from Manuscript Mode now works in character, location, item, and chapter description fields too. Pick a palette color or a custom one, right-click a selection to highlight it, and your existing yellow highlights are untouched.

**Chapter Notes on Your Index Cards** - The Corkboard's cards can now show your Chapter Notes (the chapter page's Notes field, renamed for clarity), and you can write them right on the card, with bold and italic on their usual keyboard shortcuts. Cards also size themselves to what you've chosen to show, so hiding a detail tightens the board instead of leaving blank paper. The one-line "in which" summary now keeps to 100 characters; the notes are the place for longer thinking.

**Read a Note Without Leaving the Page** - Clicking a note linked to a Notebook Block used to throw you over to the Notebook, losing your place on the character or scene you were working on. The note now opens right inside the block with a Back button, and Penpoint remembers which note you had open. An "Open notes in" switch in Edit Mode brings back the old behavior if you'd rather.

**Hide Empty Blocks** - A new cog menu option on the chapter page can tuck away any block you haven't filled in yet, handy when a long layout has a handful of blocks you only reach for now and then. Empty blocks always come back the moment you switch to Edit, so there's never one you can't get at to fill in.

**Clearing a Notebook Block** - A Notebook Block used to be a one-way door: once you pointed it at a folder, tag, or note, you could swap it but never get back to empty. A trash icon now clears it for that character or scene, and picking a new one takes one click instead of two.
**Longer Location Names** - Location names can now be up to 45 characters, matching your characters, so "The Kingdom of the Northern Reaches" fits without getting cut short.

**Corkboard Cards at Larger Text Sizes** - The chapter number badge and the PLACEHOLDER label now grow along with everything else when you scale Penpoint's text up, instead of staying put while the card around them grew.

**Empty Folders Wouldn't Stay Where You Dropped Them** - Dragging an empty chapter folder around your outline, including in a Series, could drop it somewhere other than where you put it, and a folder emptied by deleting its last chapter would jump back to an old position. Folders now land, and stay, exactly where you put them. If one of yours is sitting in the wrong spot, drag it once and it'll settle for good.

**Updates Failed on Windows ARM Laptops** - Windows ARM builds were quietly dropped a couple of releases back on the assumption nobody needed them. Some of you did, and had nothing to update to. ARM builds are back for good, starting with this release.

**Character, Location, and Item Names Weren't Clickable** - In the Chapters view, including the Minipen sidebar, these names looked like links but didn't do anything when clicked. They now take you straight to that character, location, or item's page.

**Clearing a Subtitle or Summary Now Sticks** - Clearing a chapter's subtitle or its "in which" summary looked like it worked, but the old text quietly returned the next time the book loaded. Cleared now means cleared.

**Search Turned Up Characters That Didn't Match** - Searching for words like "notebook" or "folder" listed characters that had nothing to do with them. Any character carrying a Notebook Block was matching on the block's internal bookkeeping rather than on anything you'd written. Those results are gone.
**Location Nesting** - Fixed sub-locations showing at the wrong nesting level, and dragging one somewhere it can't go now shows you instead of silently doing nothing.

**Placeholder Cards Were Lost When Copying a Book Into a Series** - Corkboard placeholder cards vanished when a book was copied into a Series, with no warning. They now come across with the book, still sitting where you left them.

**Location Types No Longer Duplicate on Series Import** - Copying a book into a Series could pile up duplicate location types. Penpoint now merges them correctly, and quietly cleans up any book already affected.
**Promoting a Placeholder Left the Folder Behind** - Promoting a card that sat inside a chapter group created the new chapter outside that group. The chapter now stays in the folder the card was in.

**Corkboard Texture on Long Boards** - On books with lots of chapters, the Corkboard's paper grain stopped partway down the page and looked stretched out. It now covers the whole board evenly, however many chapters you have.

**The Corkboard** - Your chapters, laid out as index cards you can spread across the screen and rearrange by dragging. Write a one-line summary straight onto a card, pick which details each card shows, and open up a chapter's scenes right there on the board. A button at the top of the Chapters page switches between the Corkboard and the usual view, and Penpoint remembers which one you were in.

**Placeholder Cards** - You know something happens between Chapter 4 and Chapter 5, you just don't know what yet. Drop a placeholder there: a sticky note that holds the spot on your Corkboard and in your outline without claiming a chapter number, and without ever showing up in your manuscript, your exports, or your search results. Jot the idea down, and when it firms up, promote it into a real chapter with everything you wrote already filled in.

**Notebook Block** - A new block for character sheets and chapters that shows notes from your Notebook right on the page. Link a single note to keep a backstory or beat sheet in view while you write, or link a folder or a group of tags to pull in everything related, updating automatically as your Notebook grows.

**Per-Book Word Counts in a Series** - The stats dropdown now breaks your word count down by book when you're writing a Series, and the word count in Manuscript Mode's bottom bar shows only the book you're currently in instead of adding every book together.

**Hide a Chapter's Header** - Right-click a chapter's header in Manuscript Mode and choose "Hide Chapter Header" to make it read as blank: no number, title, or subtitle, just your prose. Perfect for a prologue or interlude. Bring it back anytime by right-clicking the chapter in the outline sidebar and re-checking "Show Chapter Header."

**Hide All Subtitles at Once** - A new "Show subtitles" switch in Manuscript Mode's Settings menu hides every chapter subtitle and the "Add subtitle..." prompt in one go. Nothing is deleted, so turning it back on brings every subtitle right back.

**Minipen Polish** - The Minipen sidebar in Manuscript Mode got a look and feel pass, borrowing the cleaner layout coming to the upcoming Mobile App. Lists sit better on the page, characters and items without a photo now line up neatly, and the Chapters tab expands to show your scenes right where you can jump to them.

**Named Leap Days Are Easier to Read** - On an invented calendar, a leap day like "Stargazing Night" shows in the date grid as a small star instead of a number. Their names now appear in a "Leap days in view" line beneath the grid, so you can tell your festivals apart at a glance instead of hovering each star to read it. A star borrowed from the month on either side is labelled with which month it belongs to, like "Stargazing Night (from Emberwane)".

**Clearer "Add End Date" Button** - The button that turns a single scene date into a date range used to say "Add End Time", which was misleading: it adds a whole end date, not just a time, and on most pickers there was no time field on screen at all. It now reads "Add End Date" on every calendar, and "Add End Day" on the Day counter, where the value really is a day number rather than a date.

**@Mentions Now Find Every Nickname** - When a character had more than one nickname, typing @ and reaching for a later one (not the first in the list) could come up empty. Now every nickname finds its character, no matter which one you reach for or how many you've given them.

**Long Custom Weeks Getting Cut Off** - On an invented calendar with a very long week, the last few days of a special month could spill off the edge of the date picker where you couldn't reach them. The grid now scrolls sideways so every day stays within reach.

**Series Manuscript Export Including Every Book** - Exporting your manuscript from inside a Series pulled in chapters from every book instead of just the one you were writing, with chapter numbers running together instead of starting over at Chapter 1. Exports now stay with your current book, and the export wizard names which book it's exporting so it's never mistaken for your whole Series.

**Smart Folders Breaking When You Merge or Delete Tags** - Merging or deleting a tag could quietly break any Smart Folder linked to it, leaving it empty even though your notes were always safe elsewhere. Smart Folders now follow along when you merge a tag, and gracefully become a regular folder if you delete one.
**Sideways Phone Photos** - Photos taken on phones could save rotated and cropped from the wrong spot, whether it was a profile picture or a book cover. They now come out right side up.

**Item Types Doubling Up in a Series** - After copying a book into a Series, your item types (like "Personal Items" or "Weapons") could pile up as duplicates, and an item might show a jumble of letters and numbers where its type name belongs. Penpoint now keeps just one of each type when importing, and quietly tidies up any book that already got tangled.
**Strikethrough Shortcut in Manuscript Mode** - Ctrl+Shift+X (or Cmd+Shift+X) now toggles strikethrough while writing prose, matching the rest of Penpoint.

**Introducing Series** - Your trilogy, saga, or seven-book epic can now live together as one Series with a shared cast and world. Turn a book you've already written into Book 1 (nothing is lost), then add as many new or existing books as your story needs. Characters, locations, and items are shared across every book, so you write Sherlock once and he stays current in Book 1, Book 2, and Book 3 at once, no more re-typing your entire cast for each volume. A new Series Arc view charts the threads that run through the whole saga, and a Presence setting on each character, item, and location marks which books it belongs to. Your series shows up as a single stacked card in your library that opens onto its own shelf of covers, and you can split back into standalone books anytime.

**Import Locations, Notes, and Everything Else** - The import wizard now handles all six kinds of worldbuilding: characters, locations, items, notes, chapters, and arcs. Exports round-trip cleanly too: every field, trait, image, and @mention lands back exactly where it was, whether the file was hand-written or AI-generated. The review screen shows what's found in each file and what's new before anything is written. One note: files exported by older Penpoint versions use the old format, so re-export from this version first.

**Introducing Events** - The big moments in your story finally have a home. Create an Event like "The Duel at Dawn," link it to the characters, items, and locations involved, and it shows up on every one of their pages, shared not copied, so editing it once updates it everywhere. Jot one down with just a title, or pin it to a date and chapter once the details firm up. Events keep a single shared order across your book and lay the groundwork for the upcoming Timeline, where your whole story comes together in one view.
**Archive Notes from the Editor** - You can now archive a note directly from the note editor, using the Archive button at the bottom. No need to right-click the note in your list.

**Export a Whole Notes Folder at Once** - When exporting your notes, they're now grouped by folder so you can select an entire folder with one click instead of checking each note individually. Great for exporting a specific batch of research, chapter notes, or worldbuilding references without touching everything else.

**Open .penpoint Books by Double-Clicking** - Your computer now recognizes .penpoint files, so double-clicking one opens it straight into your library. Great for sharing a book with a friend or syncing through a cloud drive. If it's a book you already have, Penpoint asks whether to update your copy (saving a backup first, so you can undo) or keep both, and tells you which version is newer. You'll also find "Export Book" and "Import Book…" in the book library's right-click menu.

**Import an Existing Book From the New Book Menu** - Starting a new book now offers a third choice alongside "Start from Scratch" and "Import a Manuscript": Import existing Penpoint book. Pick a .penpoint file and Penpoint shows you its cover and title to confirm before adding it to your library.

**Highlight in Any Color** - Manuscript Mode's highlighter used to paint one shade of yellow. Now you can pick from a full palette, mix a custom color, or stick with classic yellow, from the highlighter pen's arrow menu (recent colors included). Palette colors adjust to your theme while custom colors stay exactly as set, and you can right-click text to add or remove a highlight on the spot. Existing highlights stay yellow until you recolor them.

**Quote Marks for Every Language** - Smart Quotes now speaks more than English. Head to Settings under Autocorrect and choose how your quote marks curl: English, Finnish and Swedish, German, Polish, or French guillemets, set separately for double and single quotes. If you use guillemets, you can add spacing inside them too: « like this ». Prefer things simple? Turn Smart Quotes off entirely from the same menu.

**OpenDyslexic Accessibility Font** - There's a new Accessibility section in Settings under Interface, with one switch: Use OpenDyslexic Font. Turn it on and both the interface and your manuscript editor switch to OpenDyslexic, a typeface designed to reduce common reading errors for people with dyslexia. It overrides your regular font choices while enabled, and remembers what you had set before, so turning it off restores everything exactly as it was. Word and EPUB exports pick up the font too; PDF exports keep your regular font for now.

**EB Garamond Font** - A new font option: EB Garamond, a classic serif with an old-style, literary feel. Pick it from Settings under Interface, where the font list now previews every option in its own typeface so you can see what you're choosing. Carries over cleanly to your PDF, Word, and EPUB exports too.

**Chapters Show Their Events** - Chapters now list the Events tied to them right in the chapter header, alongside POV and status, whether the event is anchored to the whole chapter or a specific scene within it.

**Smarter Series Merge Conflict Reporting** - Merging a book into a Series now shows you exactly which fields conflicted (like Name, Importance, Type, or Number blocks) instead of silently dropping them, so you can resolve them yourself.

**Timeline Gets Series-Aware** - In a Series book, the Timeline's Focus toggle now scopes to the active book, chapter columns follow your book's own chapter order, and color-coded bands mark which chapters belong to which book. You can also grab and pan across the timeline.

**Color Your Current Line** - The current-line highlight in Manuscript Mode isn't stuck on plain gray. Turn on "Highlight current line" and you can now tint the band one of twelve theme-matched colors or a custom shade of your own, and set how strong it looks: Subtle, Medium, or Bold. Prefer the original look? Leave it on Default.

**Tidier Character and Item Lists** - When some of your characters or items have a picture and others don't, the empty ones now show a matching framed placeholder instead of a blank gap, so your list stays lined up. It's on by default; turn it off anytime from the gear menu at the top of the Characters or Items list.
**More Room on Big Screens** - The character page now stretches wider on large displays, giving your blocks more room to spread out instead of crowding into the middle.
**Keyboard Shortcuts Reference Tidied Up** - Cleaned up the keyboard shortcuts list under the Help menu so it's easier to scan, with neater columns and clearer section headings.

**A More Welcoming First-Time Setup** - First-time setup now offers two more ways to begin: bring in an existing book from a .penpoint file (with a cover preview before you commit), or skip the walkthrough and go straight to your library. Both are handy if you already use Penpoint and you're just setting up on another computer.

**Clearer Backup Storage Numbers** - Your backup stats now spell out exactly what they're counting: the backups for the book you're in, plus a running total across all your books on this device. If you use a Secondary Backup folder, you'll see its total too.
**Snappier Book Transitions** - Opening a book and returning to your library now happens a little faster, with a smoother fade in and out instead of a cut.

**A More Communicative "Saved" Menu** - Your backups already run automatically in the background and the "Saved" indicator shows when it runs. Penpoint now also speaks up in the rare case a backup can't complete (like a cloud folder where you store your backups is disconnected), with a friendly heads-up instead of staying silent. Covers both Primary Backups and your Secondary Backup folder.

**Accurate "Last Backup" Time** - Leave Penpoint open a long while and the "Last Backup" time could lag behind reality, even though backups were running right on schedule. It now refreshes the instant each backup finishes.

**Smart Quotes in More Places** - Smart quotes now kick in consistently when you type names, labels, and descriptions for story arcs, plot points, items, locations, and notes, matching how they already work everywhere else. These fields also respect your Smart Quotes on/off setting, so if you prefer straight quotes you'll get them here too.

**Demeanor is Back** - New books now include a Demeanor trait for tracking personality, in the Standard template and every genre template. You can pick more than one when it fits, like Confident and Charming at once.
**Library Help Menu** - The "Books Guide" help option on the Library screen was renamed to "Library Guide" and now opens the guide reliably.
**Long Tag Names Getting Cut Off** - In the Tags Manager and Tags Viewer, a longer tag name would get truncated with "...". Now it wraps onto multiple lines so you can read the whole thing.
**Windows Smart App Control** - Some Windows 11 PCs were blocking Penpoint from opening. Every part of the app is now signed, so it launches normally.

**Sideways Cursor Near Horizontal Lines** - The text cursor would sometimes flip to a short horizontal bar when positioned just above a horizontal line in your notes or character descriptions. It now stays a normal vertical cursor.

**Book Covers Surviving a Move Between Computers** - Pictures in a .penpoint file exported on Windows (cover art, portraits, inline images) could go missing when opened on a Mac or Linux machine. They now carry over correctly on every system. Your words were never affected.

**Nickname @Mentions** - Giving a character several nicknames (like "Holmes/Detective") and linking to one with an @mention used to insert the whole list instead of the nickname you picked. Now it shows exactly the one you chose, and falls back to the character's full name on its own if you later remove that nickname.

**Archived Notes Vanishing in New Folders** - Archiving a note inside a folder you'd never shown archived items in before would make it disappear with no way to find it again. Now the archived section opens automatically so you can see exactly where your note went.

**Cut and Enter in Chapter & Book View** - In full-chapter or whole-book view, cutting text (Ctrl+X) or pressing Enter on a selection that crossed a scene divider used to do nothing. Both work now, and your scene and chapter dividers stay put.

**Manuscript Toolbar Scroll Jump** - Clicking a formatting button (bold, lists, alignment, and others) while scrolled down in your manuscript no longer lurches the page upward. It stays exactly where you are.

**Apostrophes Now Work in Search** - Searching for a possessive like "Sarah's" used to come back empty in both the manuscript Find bar and the main search bar, since Penpoint stores curly apostrophes but search boxes expected a plain one. Both now match either kind you type, and manuscript replacements keep your curly-quote formatting instead of swapping in plain straight quotes.

**Secondary Backups No Longer Nest Inside Themselves** - If you set your Secondary Backup location to a folder that was already called "Penpoint Backups," Penpoint would tuck another "Penpoint Backups" folder inside it. It now notices and saves straight into the folder you picked.

**Character Arc Editing Broken Without Story Arcs** - If you hadn't created any Story Arcs yet, the Edit button and Ctrl+E on the Character Arcs tab did nothing at all. They now work whether or not you have Story Arcs.
**Minipen Table View Polish** - Fixed some visual glitches in the table editing popup. It also now respects view/edit mode, so you can't edit a table unless you're actually in edit mode.

**Trait Dropdown Fixes** - Archived subtraits were still showing up as options on character sheets, and the dropdown order didn't match what you'd set in Settings. Both are fixed. Archived subtraits are now hidden from the picker, and the order matches your sort preference. If a character already has an archived subtrait selected, it stays visible in their dropdown (labeled "archived") so you can clear it when you're ready.

**Dragging Blocks into Half-Width Slots** - In the Character Sheet Layout editor, dragging a full-width block into an open half-width slot would move it there but leave it full-width instead of settling into place beside its neighbor. It now resizes correctly and lands on the side you dropped it.

**Getting Stuck During the Welcome Tour** - On some dual-monitor setups, the welcome tour could freeze on the "Manuscript Mode" step with no way forward or back. It now recovers on its own and carries on.

**Demo Book Keeps Coming Back** - If you deleted the Sherlock Holmes demo book, it would reappear every time you updated Penpoint. Now if you delete it, it stays gone. You can always bring it back through the three-dot menu in your book library.

**Line Counter Going Wrong While Typing** - The "Line N of M" counter in Manuscript Mode could drift during a long typing stretch and show something impossible like "Line 806 of 781." It now stays accurate no matter how much you type.

**Spell-Check Corrections Keep Curly Apostrophes** - Choosing a spelling correction for a word with an apostrophe used to swap your curly apostrophe for a plain straight one. Corrections now keep your curly style, and the suggestion list shows the exact quote mark it's going to insert.

**Shortcuts vs. Caps Lock** - Ctrl+K, Ctrl+N, and several other keyboard shortcuts would quietly stop responding if Caps Lock was on, in both Manuscript and Worldbuilding. Fixed across every shortcut in the app, so Caps Lock no longer gets in your way.

**Notebook Right-Click Menu Near Screen Edges** - Right-click menus in the Notebook could squeeze into a tiny sliver of space when opened near the edge of the window; they now flip to the other side so nothing gets cut off.

**Notebook Folder Colors** - Coloring a folder used to just tint a faint outline instead of the whole icon. Folders now show up fully colored, you can mix a custom shade instead of only picking from presets, and choosing "No color" finally clears it instead of doing nothing.

**Backspace and Indented Paragraphs in Manuscript Mode** - Fixed indenting a paragraph with Tab spreading that indent to every paragraph you typed after it, and Backspace needing two presses to join lines instead of one.

**Tables** - You can now insert tables into any rich text area in Penpoint: notes, character and item descriptions, location pages, chapter author notes, arc details, and more. Click the grid icon in the formatting toolbar, drag to pick how many rows and columns you want (up to 6 wide and 20 tall), and click Insert Table. Each table gets a caption above it so you can name it something useful. Right-click any cell and hover over Table to add a row above or below, add a column to the left or right, or delete the row or column you're on. You can use bold, italic, bullet lists, and @mentions inside cells. One honest caveat: tables live inside Penpoint only. When you export to Word, PDF, or any other format, each table becomes a "Table: Name" placeholder, with a full list of all your tables at the end of the file.

**Pin Characters to the Top of Your List** - Right-click any character and choose "Pin to top" to lock your protagonist, main antagonist, or any key character into a permanent Pinned Characters section at the top of the sidebar. Pinned characters stay put no matter how you sort the rest of your list, and are separated from the others by a divider. Right-click again to unpin and send them back. Works in all view modes and expands into a grid when you widen the sidebar.

**Horizontal Lines in Notes and Descriptions** - You can now insert a horizontal line into any rich-text field in Penpoint: notes, character descriptions, location pages, chapter outlines, arc plot points, and more. Look for the new line icon in the toolbar. Lines export cleanly to all formats (Word, PDF, RTF, Markdown). Manuscript Mode's existing horizontal line button was also renamed to match, so the terminology is now consistent across the app.

**Type @ to Add Names in Your Manuscript** - Type `@` while writing prose and a picker pops up with your characters, locations, items, and the rest of your worldbuilding. Pick one and the name drops in as plain text. Handy when you're juggling tricky spellings and tired of misspelling your protagonist for the fortieth time. Unlike the worldbuilding `@` picker, this one inserts the name as ordinary prose: no link, no auto-attaching anyone to your scene. Bold and italic formatting carry through, so an emphasized name stays emphasized.

**Drag Text to Move It in Notes and Descriptions** - You can now highlight text in any notebook field, character description, location page, or other worldbuilding area and drag it to a new spot, just like you've always been able to in Manuscript Mode. Hold Ctrl while dragging to copy instead of move.

**Same-Day Events on Calendar Blocks** - When a scene starts and ends on the same day, the Calendar block now shows it as a single tidy entry instead of two stacked date blocks. If you have times set, it reads something like "April 24, 1891" with "8:57 AM - 2:04 PM" below it. Much cleaner for scenes that span just a few hours.
**Calendar Picker Layout** - The month and year are now centered between the navigation arrows in the calendar picker, instead of sitting off to the left with a lot of empty space.
**Mention Picker Stays Put** - The `@` autocomplete popup used to drift sideways a bit when you stopped typing. It now stays anchored to the `@` you typed.
**Create New Tag Polish** - Pressing Enter no longer overrides your color choice, the auto-suggested color now picks an unused one from your palette instead of always picking the first color.

**Quick Create (Ctrl+N) Polish** - Fixed several rough edges in the quick-create popup. Nicknames you typed for a new character were being silently discarded instead of saved. Dropdowns like Importance and Type are now visibly highlighted when you navigate them with arrow keys, especially on lighter themes where it was nearly invisible before. The item type field is now consistently labeled "Type" everywhere, and chapter notes are now consistently labeled "Chapter Notes" throughout the app.

**Minipen Width When Switching Monitors** - If you moved Penpoint from one monitor to another with a different size or resolution, the Minipen sidebar could shrink too narrow and cause your manuscript text to scroll sideways as you typed. It now snaps to the correct minimum width when you switch screens.

**Row Highlight on Wrapped Paragraphs** - On long paragraphs that wrap to multiple lines, the highlight band could drift to the wrong line in two situations: pressing End at the end of a wrapped line, and clicking right before the first letter of a wrapped line. Both now stay put where your cursor actually is.
**Minipen Scene Selector Font** - The scene list in the Minipen Chapters tab was rendering in a smaller font than everything around it. It now matches the rest of the panel.
**Text Selection in Outline Blocks** - When using Minipen, you couldn't select or copy text from Outline blocks. Now you can.

**Image Block: Minipen Display and Lightbox Captions** - In the Minipen sidebar, images set to "Contain" were being cropped into a small fixed box, cutting off your artwork. Now they show at their natural proportions. Also fixed the image lightbox ignoring your caption position preference; captions now appear above, below, or overlaid exactly as you configured.

**Chapter Tags Now Visible in Chapter View** - You can now assign tags directly to a chapter, not just to its individual scenes. The Tags block in chapter view shows a "Whole chapter" section at the top where you can manage chapter-level tags, with your scene tags still listed below as before. If no chapter tags are set, the section stays out of your way until you're in edit mode.

**Confirmation Dialogs Now Actually Wait for Your Answer** - Clicking the trash icon on an image block could delete the image before the confirmation popup even appeared, making Cancel useless. All "are you sure?" prompts across the app now properly wait for your response before doing anything.
**Chapters Tutorial** - Fixed the Chapters page tutorial failing to start and run properly in some cases.

**Story Arcs in Minipen** - The arc visualizer was getting squished into the narrow Minipen sidebar and looking like a tangle. It's now hidden there, leaving the cleaner Whole Chapter and Scenes lists to do the job.
**Item Names No Longer Get Clipped in Cards** - Items with longer names could get cut off mid-word in the Items grid, especially on cards with a photo. Names now wrap and hyphenate properly.

**Minipen Edit Mode Polish** - Fixed the formatting toolbar pushing the Minipen sidebar wider and adding a horizontal scrollbar when editing a block. Also reworked the Character edit view so the profile picture, name, nickname, and importance fields fit comfortably in the narrow sidebar instead of getting clipped.

**Image Blocks for Characters and Scenes** - Drop an Image block into your character or chapter layout to attach pictures to each character or scene. Portraits, maps, concept art, reference photos, anything visual that helps you write. Click any uploaded image to open a zoom-and-pan viewer, or right-click to export the original back to your computer with the character or scene name pre-filled. Each image has its own caption with flexible positioning (below, above, overlaid, or off); switch to Cover mode to crop every image to the same widescreen frame. Add one via Settings > Character Layout or Settings > Chapter Layout, then Add Block > Image.

**Outline Your Scenes in the Block Layout** - There's a new Outline block for your chapter layouts. Drop it into a scene for a collapsible bullet list (or numbered, your call) to sketch beats and ideas before you write them out. Tab to indent, Shift+Tab to outdent, and fold nested items away with the chevron. Collapse state sticks with the scene, and Mentions work inside so you can drop character names straight into a beat. Add one via Settings > Chapter Layout.

**Pick a Different Font for Just Your Manuscript** - Open the gear icon at the top of Manuscript Mode and pick a font from the new "Editor Font" option. It applies only to your prose, chapter titles, and chapter subtitles. Sidebars, toolbars, and settings stay on your main font. Great for writers who prefer a serif for prose but a clean sans-serif everywhere else. Pick "Use Global Font" to match the rest of the app again.

**Live Book Cover Preview** - When creating or editing a book, a preview now appears right alongside the settings so you can see exactly how your cover will look on the shelf. Change the title, pick a color, swap a texture, or upload an image, and the preview updates instantly.

**Highlight Your Current Line** - Turn on "Highlight current line" in the View settings (gear icon) to see a soft band follow your cursor as you write. The footer also shows your line number alongside the word count, and one toggle controls both. Great for finding your place after a distraction or keeping your eyes anchored during a careful reread.

**Manuscript Sidebar Polish** - Items and locations now show their icons and pictures in the sidebar, matching how they look on the main pages. Notes now support archive view (gear icon, archived items at the bottom), note tags are clickable and jump to that tag's view, and the Back button returns you to the folder you were browsing.

**Notebook Archive and Tagging Polish** - Archived notes now gather in their own "Archived" section at the bottom of each folder, and opening one shows an Unarchive banner with the content locked until you bring the note back. You can also create a new tag right from a note's tag picker without leaving the editor.

**Build Consecutive Custom Calendar Eras Faster** - Each era in your Custom Calendar now has an "Add next era" button. If the era has a duration set, the new one starts right where the last one ends. No more calculating start years by hand.
**Smoother Chapter Editing** - Switching between View and Edit mode on your Chapters page now animates smoothly instead of snapping instantly, matching the feel of Characters, Locations, and Items.

**Chapter Export Restored** - The "Export Worldbuilding" feature for chapters was broken after scenes were added to the Chapters page, showing almost nothing. Each scene now exports as its own labeled section with everything filled in: descriptions, notes, dates, characters (with POV markers), plot points, locations, items, and tags.

**Picture Export in Single-File Mode** - When exporting a compendium as a single file, pictures (profile images and Image block contents) now export to a `<filename>-images/` folder alongside the document. Single-file mode was silently skipping the export-pictures toggle; both modes now export consistently.

**"Where I Left Off" Now Saves Reliably** - If you closed Penpoint while writing without switching chapters first, your cursor position sometimes wasn't remembered. Now it saves as you go, so "Where I Left Off" always puts you back in the right spot.

**Adding a Scene Renaming Your Other Scenes** - If you had scenes without custom titles and added a new scene via right-click in the Manuscript outline, Penpoint would rename all your untitled scenes to generic labels like "Scene 4", "Scene 5", etc. Those scenes now keep showing their opening lines as a preview.

**Missing Cover Options When Importing a Manuscript** - The final setup screen in the manuscript import flow was missing texture, custom color, and cover image options. The import experience now matches creating a book from scratch, preview included.

**Manuscript Import Duplicates** - When importing a manuscript, the scanner could list the same character or place twice if the only difference was capitalization (like "the Briars" and "The Briars"). They now merge into a single entry with the combined count.
**Duplicating a Book Now Copies Everything** - When you duplicated a book with a cover image or custom color, those didn't carry over to the copy. Both now copy correctly.

**Chapter Break Now Names Chapters Correctly** - Using the Chapter break button in the toolbar and leaving the title blank would stamp your new chapter with "Untitled Chapter" instead of a proper number. It now matches the behavior of creating a chapter from the left panel.

**Notebook Note Fixes** - Creating a new tag from a note's tag picker now works in both the Notebook and the Manuscript sidebar. Long note titles wrap properly at larger text sizes instead of getting cut off. Tag pills in the note footer now match the bordered style used throughout the app.
**Empty Trait Blocks** - Trait blocks for traits with no subtraits no longer hang on "Loading..."; they now show "None" in view mode and a shortcut link to configure that trait in edit mode.

**Location Icon Now Visible Next to Type** - If a location had a profile picture, its icon would disappear from the detail panel. The icon now also appears next to the "Type" field, so you can always see it whether or not a picture is set.

**Pick Chapters by the Scene** - When adding a character, item, location, or plot point to a chapter, you can now see and pick exactly which scenes to assign. Chapters with multiple scenes expand in the picker — tick the whole chapter to add to everything at once, or pick individual scenes. Already-assigned entries are hidden, and the Manuscript Mode sidebars now also show which scenes you've tagged under each chapter.

**Eras for Custom Calendars** - Custom calendars now support a full era system. In Calendar Settings, choose how dates display: plain years, a BCE/CE-style split with your own before/after labels, or named eras with their own start dates like "Reign of King Valdris." Pick from four date phrasings and your dates use that style throughout the app. Gaps between eras fall back to a Base era automatically, so you don't need to account for every stretch of unrecorded time.

**Copy Blocks Across Scenes** - Right-click any block in a multi-scene chapter — a date, character list, location, description, or anything else — and copy it to all other scenes at once. Or choose "Copy all blocks to all scenes" to sync your entire scene's data across every scene in the chapter. A confirmation dialog shows which scene you're copying from before anything changes.

**Penpoint Startup Safety Net** - In the rare event Penpoint can't start, you'll see a clear screen confirming your books are safe, with buttons to restart, email support, or save a log file to attach to your message.

**Arc Plot Point Rework** - Adding a plot point is now one searchable dropdown instead of two clicks. Type "climax" and every arc's climax shows up in a single list — tick more than one at a time. On the Chapters page, what used to be two competing Story Arcs sections is now one block with clear "Whole chapter" and per-scene sub-sections.

**Chapter-Wide Plot Points** - Restored the ability to assign plot points to an entire chapter separately from individual scenes. Removing a chapter-level plot point no longer touches scene-level ones. Chapters and scenes can share the same plot points or have their own.

**Cleaner Detail Pages** - On Location pages, "Characters & Items" is now split into separate Characters and Items sections, each with its own search. The Add buttons on Item and Location pages got a quieter look — a dashed row sitting at the bottom of each list.

**Scene Descriptions and Notes Could Disappear** - On rare occasions, the Description and Notes blocks on chapter scenes could go empty when interacting with arc assignments. Fixed at the source, with added safeguards so this can't happen again. If you've been affected, your text is safe in your automatic backups — message us on Discord and we'll walk you through restoring it.

**Undo for Accidental Scene Merges** - Accidentally merged two scenes with Backspace? Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on Mac) now brings the absorbed scene back fully intact: title, color, status, custom fields, and assignments. Works for right-click merges too.
**Deleting a Scene Now Refreshes Instantly** - Deleted scenes no longer linger in the Manuscript navigator and editor. They disappear right away everywhere, as they should.
**Export From the Book Library** - Right-clicking a book and choosing "Export" wasn't working. Now it opens a save dialog so you can save your book as a `.penpoint` backup file wherever you like.
**Enter Key in Chapter Picker** - Hitting Enter on a highlighted chapter or scene now adds it and closes the popup, as expected. Previously it required a separate tick first.
**Editing Book Cover Could Lock the Save Button** - If you uploaded a cover image for the first time without changing anything else, the Save Changes button would stay grayed out. Fixed!
**Backup Imports Could Show Outdated Book Settings** - Reimporting a `.penpoint` backup could occasionally restore an older book cover. Your most recent covers now always travel with the backup.
**Full Version History in the App** - Settings > About now has a "See past versions" button. Click it to browse every version's release notes without leaving Penpoint.

**The Chapters Page, Reimagined** - One of Penpoint's most-requested features is finally here. The Chapters page has been rebuilt from the ground up. Each chapter now has its own customizable block-based layout — just like Character Sheets — so you can design a chapter view that fits how *you* plan stories. Every scene now stands on its own with its own characters, locations, items, and POV (tags and arcs stay at the chapter level, where they belong). The new outliner sidebar mirrors Manuscript Mode, so navigating between chapters and scenes feels instantly familiar. Configure your default scene layout in Settings → Scene Layout. Your existing chapters carry over with their current view intact — nothing to redo.

**Build Your Own World's Calendar** - Your book now has its own calendar system. Pick **Standard (Gregorian)** for real-world stories, **Day Counter** for stories told by day number ("Day 47" instead of "March 12"), or go wild with **Custom** and design a fantasy calendar from scratch: your own months, weekdays, festival periods, leap days, even BCE/CE-style epochs. Every scene and chapter date uses your chosen mode automatically. This also paves the way for a FUTURE rework of the Timeline view.

**Customize Your Character Arc View** - The Character Arc page now has a gear icon in the visualizer header to control what's visible. Choose to show plot points for all characters, just the active one, or none at all. Toggle "Always show labels" off for a clean comparison view — you can still hover or click any keyframe to reveal its label. The active character's line is also a bit thicker now so it stands out from any overlays. **Plus**: you can now assign chapters (and specific scenes) to individual plot points on character arcs, just like story arcs. Open any plot point in edit mode to link chapters, or switch to view mode to see them as a read-only list. Linked chapters also show up in the compact list view on the arc block itself.

**Customize Your Book Covers** - Your books on the shelf just got a lot more personal. Pick from 12 preset colors or mix your own with a built-in color picker. Layer on a texture like Grain, Linen, Leather, or Parchment for that hardcover feel. Or go all out and upload your own cover image, cropped to fit. If your image already has the title on it, you can hide Penpoint's text overlay so it doesn't compete. All your choices travel with your book through backups and restores.

**Search Works in Manuscript Mode** — The Glorious Searchbar popup (Ctrl+K) now works while you're writing, not just in Worldbuilding. Search for a character, location, item, chapter, or anything else — clicking a result opens it in your Minipen sidebar without taking you away from your manuscript. Scene results jump you straight to that scene in the editor.

**See Where Your Locations Appear** - Every location now shows which chapters it appears in, right on its detail page. Open "The Haunted Library" and see at a glance that it shows up in Chapters 3, 7, and 12. In edit mode, you can assign or remove chapter connections directly from the location itself.

**Version Protection for Your Books** - If you open a book on one computer with a newer version of Penpoint, then try to open it on another running an older version, Penpoint will tell you exactly what's happening and ask you to update before opening the book.
**New "Alice" Theme** - A soft cherry blossom pink theme for those who like their writing space a little more lovely. Find it in Settings → Interface alongside the other themes.
**Reset the Demo Book** - The Sherlock Holmes demo book now has a Reset option in its right-click menu. Restore it to its original state any time you want a clean tour.

**Find Characters by Their Nickname** - Anywhere you add a character to something (a scene, a relationship, an item, a location, a chapter, or an arc), you can now search by their alias instead of their full name. Type "Lizzy" and Elizabeth Bennet shows up.

**Filter Items by Location** - You can now filter your Items list by location. Select one or more locations in the filter sidebar and only items tied to those locations will show. Works the same as your other filters.

**Smoother Startup Experience** - If you haven't opened Penpoint in a while, you might have a few things waiting: an update, a data upgrade, maybe an announcement. They now queue up and appear one at a time in a sensible order, so you're never overwhelmed by overlapping pop-ups. The analytics prompt also has a new "Not now" option.
**Refreshed Chapters Tutorial** - The Chapters tutorial has been rewritten to walk you through the new block-based layout, with clearer steps and better example data.
**Tag Viewer for Multi-Scene Chapters** - The Tag Viewer now works properly across chapters with multiple scenes, showing tags at the right level so you can see what's tagged where without confusion.

**Keyboard Navigation in Notebook and Items** - Arrow keys now move to the visually adjacent card instead of jumping alphabetically, and Alt+Left/Alt+Right cleanly goes back or forward without also shifting your highlight. The Items page also picked up Up and Down arrow keys for jumping between rows.

**Every Word Counts** - The community word count in your stats panel now shows every word written in Penpoint since launch, right down to the last one. We just crossed a million, and watching that number climb is a lot more fun when you can see it tick upward.

**Chapter Descriptions Preserved Across Upgrades** - Fixed an upgrade path where chapter descriptions could be lost when migrating to the new block-based chapter layout. Every upgrade path now preserves your chapter descriptions completely.

**Character Arc Overlays Lining Up** - When comparing multiple character arcs, plot point markers on background arcs could drift out of alignment with the active character's, even when both arcs had the same number of points. They line up properly now.

**Crosslinks Now Show Scenes** - Items, Locations, and Characters that appear in chapters now drill down to specific scenes, not just the chapter as a whole. Character chapter lists also show the correct scene numbers (instead of internal positions), and Story Arc plot points correctly filter to their assigned scenes in view mode.

**Arc Scene Assignment Clarity** - Assigned scenes in your arc plot points now show a filled square so you can see at a glance what's linked. The Assign and Remove buttons are always visible, no hovering required.

**Right-Click Submenus Staying on Screen** - Fixed several cases where right-click submenus could get cut off at the screen edge, especially near a corner. When a submenu flips to the opposite side to fit, it now sits flush against the parent menu instead of overlapping or leaving a gap.

**Cleaner Scene Names** - Adding a second scene to a chapter no longer leaves you with two rows labeled "Empty Scene". New scenes are now named "Scene 1", "Scene 2", and so on. Scenes you've already named are left alone.

**Duplicate Scenes Under Rapid Clicking** - Fixed a rare race condition where rapid clicks during scene creation could occasionally create duplicate or orphaned scenes. Scene creation is now reliable even under heavy clicking.
**Calendar and Chapter Card Polish** - Several calendar UI improvements and chapter card display fixes, plus better submenu positioning throughout.

**Notebook Rename Fixes** - Fixed two rename issues: renaming a folder in the sidebar could fail if that same folder was visible in the main grid at the same time (the rename box would flash and disappear before you could type), and renaming a note while it was open in the viewer didn't refresh the title inside the editor until you switched notes.

**Export Title Page Remembers Your Book** - The Title field in the manuscript export dialog now always shows your current book's name, not whatever you last exported. If you've customized the title before, Penpoint remembers your custom version per book.

**Location Renames Now Update the List** - Renaming a location in edit mode didn't update the name in the left-hand list until you reloaded the app. Now the list updates on its own right after you stop typing, and the title field feels snappier too.

**Faster Search Results After Editing** - If you fixed a word in your manuscript and then searched for it, the old version could still show up in search results for several seconds. Now results update the moment you open the searchbar.
**Manuscript Cursor Hiding Behind Toolbar** — The typing cursor could scroll up behind the formatting toolbar, letting you type text you couldn't see. Fixed.
**Domain URLs in Manuscripts** - Fixed a rare bug where domain endings like .it could sneak into your manuscript as hidden links. Your text is now safe from sneaky URLs.
**Cutting Text No Longer Reduces Your Word Count** — Using cut and paste to move text around no longer affects your daily word count.
**Word Count Stats After Midnight** — If you were writing past midnight, the "Manuscript size (+X today)" line in your daily stats could show the wrong number. Fixed.

**Manuscript Folders Staying Put** - If you made a few empty folders in Manuscript Mode's chapter outliner back to back and dragged them into order, they could quietly swap positions when you came back later. Now they stay exactly where you put them.
**Notebook Panel Widths Drifting** — If you resized the folder tree or preview panel in the Notebook and then switched to another page and came back, the panels would shift slightly each time. Fixed.
**Back Button Not Clearing Item Selection** - On the Items page, pressing Back right after selecting an item didn't actually deselect it, which threw off the back and forward history. Fixed.
**Search Result Highlights on Hover** — When hovering over a search result, the matched search term could become hard to read. Fixed.

**Closing the App During the Welcome Tour** - The X button now properly closes Penpoint during the first-run welcome tour. Before, you'd have to wait for the tour to finish (or force-quit) to get out.
**Historical / Non-fiction Template** - Renamed the "Historical" New Book template to "Historical / Non-fiction" for better discoverability.

**Chapter Drafts** — Scene Drafts now work for chapters that haven't been split into multiple scenes. Right-click any single-scene chapter in the outline and you'll find "Chapter Drafts" — save a snapshot, view old versions, or restore a previous draft, same as always. If you later split the chapter into scenes, your saved drafts carry over automatically. Nothing is lost.

**Find & Replace with Formatting** — The Find & Replace bar now has a collapsible "Advanced" section at the bottom. Use **Match** to narrow your search to only bold, italic, or underlined text — perfect for tracking down foreign words or specific styled passages. Use **Apply** to add formatting to your replacements, like swapping a nickname for an italicized foreign name in one operation. Works with Replace All and "Replace in rest of manuscript" too.

**Whole Word Matching in Find & Replace** — A new toggle in Find & Replace lets you match whole words only — so searching for "Yes" won't accidentally catch "Yesterday" or "Yes-terday". It's on by default. Penpoint remembers all your Find & Replace settings between sessions, so everything's exactly where you left it next time you open it.

**Find & Replace Button in the Toolbar** — There's now a magnifying glass button in the manuscript toolbar that opens and closes Find & Replace. It stays highlighted while the panel is open, so you always know at a glance whether it's active.

**Notebook Display Fixes** — Fixed the note editor panel overflowing off-screen when the navigation sidebar was pinned, and fixed note titles in list view squishing to a few characters per line at high display scaling.

**Flowstate No Longer Forces Fullscreen** — Starting a Flowstate session used to automatically push you into fullscreen mode, and ending it would pull you back out. Now the two are independent — run Flowstate in your normal view, or combine it with fullscreen. Your call.

**Find & Replace Stays in Sync When Switching Chapters** — If you had Find & Replace open and switched to a different chapter or scene, the results would still show matches from the old chapter. Now it automatically re-searches the new content and clears any previous replace counts.
**Smart Quotes After Punctuation** — Typing a quote mark after a period or other punctuation could produce a straight quote instead of a curly one. Fixed.
**Curly Quotes After Em Dashes** — Quote marks after an em dash could face the wrong direction when ending interrupted dialogue. Fixed.

**Minipen Notes Sorting** — Fixed sorting in the Minipen Notes sidebar: numbered folders now sort naturally (1, 2, 10 instead of 1, 10, 2), changing the sort order updates the list immediately, and the sort menu now matches the layout used elsewhere in the app.
**Honoring Penpoint's First Purchase** — The About page now recognizes Jendriel as Penpoint's Founding Supporter — the very first person to buy a license. Thank you!

**Zen Mode for Manuscripts** — Press F11 or click "Fullscreen Mode" in the footer to fade away the toolbar, sidebars, and header over a smooth 2.5-second transition — just you and your words. Hover the screen edges to slide out the chapter outline or Minipen as overlays, or hover the top to drop down the formatting toolbar on demand. New Settings options under **Fullscreen Mode** let it activate automatically when you start typing and exit after 30 seconds idle — Flowstate also triggers it.

**The Worldbuilding Toolbar Guide** — A new help article walks you through every icon and button in the toolbar — the save indicator, writing stats, help menu, announcements bell, clock, and more. Find it in the User Guide under "The Worldbuilding Toolbar."

**Restoring Backups Got a Big Upgrade** — Backup history is now accessible from three places: the Book Selector, Settings > Storage & Backups, and the "Saved" dropdown in the toolbar. When you restore, you choose how: **Overwrite Current Book** (recommended — replaces your book in place) or **Restore as New Book** (creates a separate copy so nothing gets replaced). Either way, Penpoint automatically creates a safety backup first, so you can always undo a restore if you change your mind.

**Total Word Count in the Footer** — The word count bar at the bottom of Manuscript Mode now shows your current scope alongside your total manuscript word count — so you can see "1,234 words (50,000 total)" at a glance without opening the stats panel. Click the word count to hide the total if you prefer a cleaner look. Penpoint remembers your preference.
**Right-Click Anywhere in Your Outline** — You can now right-click on empty space in the Manuscript outline to quickly add a new chapter or group — no need to reach for the + button.

**Notebook Folder Drag-and-Drop** — Improved drag-and-drop for folders in the Notebook — you can now drag folders between levels, out of subfolders, and into new positions with cleaner visual feedback.

**Faster Note Creation in the Notebook** — Creating a new note now drops your cursor right into the title field so you can start typing immediately. Press Tab to jump straight into the writing area — no clicking required.

**User Guide on Smaller Screens** — The Help Guide is now much more readable on smaller screens and narrower windows. The article index adjusts automatically so your help articles always have room to breathe.
**Dragging Notes & Folders to the Binder Deleted Them** — Dragging a note or folder from the main area into the Binder (the root level of your Notebook) would make it vanish. Fixed.

**Undo in the Notebook** — Pressing Ctrl+Z in a note when there was nothing left to undo could replace your entire note with whatever was in the previous note you had open. Fixed — undo now only applies to changes you made in the current note.

**Item Titles Overwriting Each Other** — If you edited an item's title and quickly clicked another item before the save finished, the first item's new title would get written onto the second item instead. Fixed — saves now always go to the right item, no matter how fast you click.

**Character-Item Relationship Notes Disappearing** — If you typed a note describing how a character relates to an item and switched to view mode too quickly, the note would vanish. Fixed — it now always saves before the switch.

**Editing a Trait Option Now Updates Your Characters** — If you fixed a typo in a trait option (like correcting "Bule" to "Blue"), any character already assigned that value would be stuck showing the old one — and you couldn't clear it without a workaround. Now renaming a trait option updates all your characters automatically.

**Typing on macOS Sequoia** — macOS Sequoia's autocorrect could silently rewrite words while you typed, causing cursor jumps and random duplicate text. Penpoint now disables system-level autocorrect within the editor to prevent this. Your smart quotes and dash settings still work exactly as before.

**@Mention Fixes** — Fixed several @mention bugs: Escape now closes the suggestion popup without deleting what you typed, custom item types now show their real names instead of ID numbers, the Home key no longer jumps to the wrong line when a line starts with a mention, and punctuation right after a mention link (like a comma) no longer orphans to the next line. You can also now press Tab to confirm a suggestion.

**Items Uneditable After Filtering by Tags** — If you filtered your Items list by specific tags and then created a new item, the item would immediately vanish from view and couldn't be edited — Ctrl+E did nothing, and the Edit button was unresponsive. Fixed — the detail panel now stays open so you can fill in the item's details before it shows up in your filtered view.

**Minipen Search Now Takes You to the Right Spot** — Clicking a scene result in the Minipen search would open the right scene but drop you at the top instead of at the text you searched for. It now jumps straight to your match and highlights it.

**Daily Word Count Now Reflects Real Progress** — Deleted words now subtract from your daily word count. If you rewrote a sentence, it no longer counts the original words *and* the rewrite — you see the actual net change for the day. This means your word count can go negative if you spent the day cutting, which is an honest look at a heavy editing session.

**Unnumbered Chapters Showing Wrong Numbers in @Mentions** — If you marked a chapter as unnumbered (a prologue, interlude, or epilogue), @mentioning it would still display it as "Chapter 4: Prologue" or similar. It now shows just the chapter title, and numbered chapters that follow show the correct sequential number.

**Writing Stats Resetting at Midnight** — If you write past midnight, your daily word count delta (the "+350 today" next to your manuscript size) would silently disappear until you restarted the app. It now resets automatically at midnight like it should.

**Writing Streak Showing Wrong Numbers** — Your writing streak could get stuck showing the wrong count after opening the app. Fixed the underlying cause and made the streak calculation more resilient.

**Character List Scrolling Back Into Position** — When you returned to your character list after visiting another page, Penpoint would scroll through the whole list to get back to where you were instead of jumping straight there. Fixed — it now snaps immediately to your last selected character.
**Item Type Dropdown Not Updating** — Changing an item's type while in edit mode would tick the right checkbox but the label wouldn't update until you left edit mode. Fixed — it updates immediately.

**Empty Folders Now Stay Where You Put Them** — Dragging an empty folder to a new spot in your outline would snap it right back the moment you let go. Fixed — empty folders now stay wherever you drop them.
**Smart Quotes & Backspace** — When smart quotes were on, backspace would first convert a curly quote back to a straight quote before deleting it — requiring two presses instead of one. Fixed.
**Relationships Block at Half-Width** — Fixed relationship entries spreading apart with large gaps when the block is placed side-by-side with another block.
**Writing Stats Panel Getting Cut Off** — On some screens, the writing stats dropdown could extend past the edge of the window, clipping the text and button. Fixed.
**Notebook Text Overflowing After Paste** — Pasting text into a Notebook note could cause content to run off the right edge of the screen instead of wrapping properly. Fixed.

**Right-Click Menus on Chapters, Items & Locations** — Chapters, Items, and Locations now all have full right-click menus. Right-click a chapter card to open it, jump to the Manuscript editor, reorder, insert a new chapter before or after, or delete. Right-click items or locations to add, delete, change importance, sort, and more. Detail panels have their own right-click menus too — quick access to edit mode, profile image, type changes, and other common actions without hunting through the UI.

**Writing Stats: Manuscript Size & Last Writing Day** — Your analytics dropdown (the chart icon in the toolbar) now shows your current manuscript word count with today's change — great for tracking editing progress toward a target — plus a quick look at how your last writing day went, so picking up after a break you can see at a glance what you accomplished last time you sat down.

**Sort Locations Ascending or Descending** — The Locations sort menu now includes Ascending and Descending options, so you can flip any sort method — alphabetical Z to A, newest first, or reverse type order.
**Credit Where Credit Is Due** — Check out Settings → About for a little something new. You know who you are.

**Opening a Chapter in Manuscript Mode Now Goes to the Right Chapter** — The first time you opened a chapter in Manuscript from the Chapters page, it would load whichever chapter you had open last instead of the one you clicked. Second click would work. Fixed — it goes to the right chapter every time now.

**Multi-Value Traits Lost on Import** — If a character had a trait with multiple values selected (e.g., "Brave" and "Trustworthy"), importing that character would collapse them into a single combined value instead of two separate ones. Fixed.
**Typing Glitch on Mac** — On some Macs, the cursor could suddenly jump to the start of a sentence and drag text along with it while you were typing. Fixed.

**Character List Expanding to Full Screen** — When you clicked the arrow to expand your character list to fill the whole screen, it would stay in a single column instead of spreading out across the space. Fixed — it now fills the width with as many columns as will fit.

**Deleted Items Staying on Screen** — Deleting an item would remove its card from the list, but the detail panel would stay open showing the deleted item as if it were still there. Now the panel closes cleanly when an item is deleted.

**Spellcheck Flagging Possessives of Character Names** — Penpoint auto-whitelists your characters, locations, and items in the spellchecker — but writing "Charlye's" (possessive) would still get flagged as a spelling error even though "Charlye" was fine. Fixed.

**Autocorrect Settings** — New controls under Settings → Spellcheck & Autocorrect let you choose your dash behavior (**Standard**: `--` → em dash, or **Typographer**: `--` → en dash, `---` → em dash) and toggle smart curly quotes on or off.
**Chapter Titles Are Now Optional** — Leave the title blank when creating a chapter and it shows up as "Chapter 1", "Chapter 2", etc. Add a title whenever you're ready — or never.

**Copy Text from the Compendium and Help Guide** — You can now highlight and copy text in the Compendium and Help Guide. Help Guide navigation links are also now a distinct color so they're easier to spot at a glance.

**Strikethrough in Manuscript** — Strikethrough was missing from the Manuscript toolbar (and its keyboard shortcut didn't work either). It's now available alongside Bold, Italic, Underline, and Highlight. The text highlighter also now looks identical in both Manuscript and your worldbuilding notes — same shade, same size, visible on dark themes.

**Chapter Outline Changes Appearing Deleted** — Editing a chapter outline and switching to another section could make your recent changes appear to vanish. Your work was saved the whole time — it was a display glitch. Fixed.

**Book Scanner Accuracy** — The scanner was occasionally linking characters, locations, and items to the wrong chapters, and could show duplicate aliases in results. Matching is now more precise, and nicknames saved during import work correctly with @mentions.

**Tags Now Work in Quick Create** — The Tags block in Quick Create (Ctrl+N) now shows your tags as selectable options when creating a new character. Click to add, click again to remove — all applied when you hit Create.
**Timeline Not Scrolling** — If you had enough characters to fill the Timeline vertically, the rest were cut off with no way to reach them. The Timeline now scrolls.
**Scene Drafts Preserved After Versioning** — Fixed scene drafts going missing after creating a manuscript version. Both features now stay completely independent.
**Spellcheck False Positives on Quoted Words** — Words in single quotes (like 'this') were getting flagged by spellcheck even when spelled correctly. Fixed.
**Spellcheck Underlines Hidden in View Mode** — Spellcheck squiggles now only appear when you're actively editing. In view mode, they stay out of the way.

**Novel View No Longer Indents Centered Text** — The "Novel" paragraph setting adds a first-line indent to your prose, but was also indenting centered and right-aligned text. Those are now left alone.
**Tags Section Card Previews** — Entity cards in the Tags section could show raw code for cleared fields, and @mentions in descriptions were dropped entirely. Both fixed.

**Discord Status Stuck on "Worldbuilding Mode"** — Opening Penpoint directly into Manuscript Mode would show "Worldbuilding Mode" in your Discord status until you navigated somewhere. Your status now reflects where you actually are from the moment you open the app.
**Manuscript Tutorial Freezing at Step 3** — On high-resolution or custom-scaled displays, the Manuscript Tutorial could get stuck at Step 3 when selecting a chapter. Fixed.
**Character List Scrolling on Return** — Navigating back to the Characters section would trigger a scroll animation down to your selected character. Now it jumps there instantly.
**Notebook Back Button Now Returns to Root** — The back button in the Notebook now treats the root level as a proper stop in navigation history, so you can always get back to where you started.
**Tutorial Polish** — Thanks to great feedback from CovOp and Tapgiles on Discord, we've fixed a variety of bugs across many tutorial walkthroughs.
**Items Tutorial Restart Not Appearing** — The "Restart Tutorial" option was missing from the Help menu on the Items page. Fixed.
**Manuscript Toolbar Button Spacing** — Two toolbar buttons could end up jammed together at certain window widths. Fixed.
**Notebook Right-Click Menu Positioning** — Right-clicking near screen edges could cause the context menu to flicker into place or appear far from your cursor. Fixed.

**Relationship Block Swap Roles** — Two-way relationships with different labels can now display in either order. By default, each name shows the role they play *for* the current character. Flip on "Swap Role Labels" in the Relationships block settings to pair each name with their own role instead.

**Onboarding on Small Screens** — The new-user walkthrough could look broken on smaller screens or at larger font sizes. The entire flow is now responsive, scaling from compact laptops to 4K displays.

**Profile Picture Cropping** — The crop dialog for character, item, and location images wasn't working — overflow, unresponsive drag/zoom, and hidden buttons. Fixed, and the crop window now adapts to portrait and landscape images instead of a fixed square.

**Searchbar Overlapping Toolbar Buttons** — At narrower window widths, the search bar would drift into the right-side toolbar buttons, covering the + button, the save indicator, and more. Now it slides left into the space near the navigation arrows to keep everything visible.

**Character & Notebook Images Not Displaying** — Profile pictures, notebook images, and inline manuscript images could all appear broken after updating to v1.0.23. Your images were never lost — a security policy was blocking the app from displaying them. All images now load correctly again.

**Import a Manuscript When Creating a Book** — When creating a new book, you can now choose "Import a Manuscript" instead of starting from scratch. Pick your file, preview and customize your chapters, optionally scan the whole manuscript for characters, locations, and items, then name your book and go. Everything — your prose, your chapters, and any discovered story elements — lands in your new book ready to work with.

**Half-Width Blocks for Every Block Type** — You can now place any block side-by-side on your character sheet layout — not just Traits and Numbers. Tags next to a Character Arc. Appearance paragraph next to Age. Whatever makes sense for your characters. Click the new split-column icon in a block's toolbar to toggle it half-width, and click again to expand it back.

**Spellcheck in Worldbuilding** *(Beta)* — Spellcheck now works in your character, location, and item notes — not just in Manuscript Mode. Right-click an underlined word for suggestions or to add it to your dictionary, same as always.

**Character Page Right-Click Menus** — Right-click anywhere on the Characters page for quick access to common actions. Right-click a character in the list to add, delete, or change sort/view options. Right-click a character's detail panel to toggle edit mode, change importance, swap the profile image, jump to the Relationship Map, edit their sheet layout, and more — all without hunting through menus.
**Manuscript Right-Click Menu** — Undo, Redo, Select All, and Paste without Formatting are now in the right-click context menu. Paste also now correctly preserves bold, italic, and other formatting.

**Smarter Help Guide Search** — The search bar in the Help Guide now searches the full content of every article — not just titles. Find what you're looking for even if you only remember a word or phrase from inside the article. Results show the article name, the section where the match was found, and a highlighted snippet so you can tell at a glance if it's the right one.

**Revamped Tutorials** — Every interactive tutorial across Penpoint has been overhauled. Tooltips now point exactly where they should, example data is more realistic, and the Notebook page gets its own full walkthrough for the first time. No more stuck tooltips or empty panels during the tour.
**Expanded New User Walkthrough** — The new author experience has been polished and expanded with new slides, smoother animations, and better guidance so you feel right at home from the start.

**Manuscript Import & Export in Settings** — You can now import and export your manuscript prose directly from the Import & Export settings page — no need to open Manuscript Mode first. The page is also reorganized into Worldbuilding and Manuscript sections, so everything has its place.
**Em Dash Shortcut** — Three dashes (`---`) now make an em dash automatically.
**Content Scanner Crash on Older Macs** — Fixed a crash that prevented the content scanner from running on macOS Monterey (12.x) and earlier.

**Manuscript Search Now Actually Works** — Searching for text from your manuscript wasn't showing any results, even when the text was right there. Fixed. The Minipen sidebar search also now shows a preview of the matching passage so you can confirm it's the right scene before clicking.

**Custom Dictionary Words Not Sticking** — Adding a word to your custom dictionary could appear to work (it showed up in the list) but the red underline wouldn't go away. Also fixed: custom words would vanish after a full restart — they'd still be in the list but spellcheck would ignore them until you switched languages and back.

**Character Import Losing Long-Text Content** — When importing character files, fields like Backstory could come in empty if the content used bold section headings (like **Early Life:** or **Blake's birth:**). All that text is now imported correctly.

**Scanner Missing Names at Sentence Starts** — The content scanner wasn't finding character names that appeared mostly at the beginning of sentences. It would only catch the name once you added enough mid-sentence uses. Now one mid-sentence mention is enough — the scanner correctly counts all occurrences.

**Minipen Location Dropdowns Not Updating** — Changing a location's icon, importance, type, or parent ("Part of") in the Minipen sidebar would appear to snap back to the old value. Your change was actually saving — you just couldn't see it until you switched back to View mode. Fixed.

**Discord Status Haunting Your Profile** — Closing Penpoint didn't always clear your Discord Rich Presence status, so your friends might think you're still writing at 3 AM. Penpoint now properly tells Discord "I'm done" on exit instead of ghosting the connection.
**Deleted Characters Staying in Spellcheck** — Deleting a character, location, or item now properly clears their name from the spellcheck dictionary.

**Help Guide Not Knowing You're in Settings** — The context-aware Help button now correctly shows the right guide when you're in a Settings subcategory. Before, it would send you to the guide for whatever page you were on *before* opening Settings.
**Manuscript Importer: Better Title Page Handling** — When importing a Word document, content before the first chapter now shows the document's title (or "Title Page") rather than the filename.

**Spellcheck** *(Beta)* — Your manuscript now checks spelling as you write, with red underlines on unrecognized words. Right-click any underline for suggestions or to add the word to your personal dictionary. Characters, locations, and items are automatically whitelisted so your invented names are never flagged. Manage dictionaries and settings in Settings → Spellcheck.

**Discord Rich Presence** — Optionally show your writing activity in your Discord status. Enable it in Settings → Community & Updates and your friends will see what you're working on. Your writing content is never shared — only which section you're in. Requires the Discord desktop app to be running.

**Collapsible Sections Everywhere** — The collapsible section headers from the Character Sheet are now on Items, Locations, and Chapters too — including their Minipen sidebars. Click any section header to tuck it away; preferences are remembered per page.

**Set Numbered/Unnumbered at Chapter Creation** — You can now uncheck "Numbered chapter" right in the creation dialog — no need to create it first and hunt down the toggle. The chapter number preview updates live.
**Terms of Service & Privacy Policy** — You'll see a one-click agreement prompt the first time you launch after updating. Everything you write still belongs to you, always.

**Hardware Acceleration Toggle** — If you're experiencing visual glitches, disable hardware acceleration in Settings → Advanced. Penpoint restarts in software rendering mode. Most useful on Windows with integrated graphics.

**Content Scanner Upgrades** — A new whole-manuscript scan reviews all your chapters at once — finding known characters, locations, and items, discovering new ones, and linking everything to the right chapters in one pass. No more chapter-by-chapter scanning. Trigger it by right-clicking your book title in the outline sidebar, or it runs automatically after a manuscript import. Location and item detection has also improved.

**Find & Replace Upgrades** — Both fields are now always visible (no toggle needed), and your last search and replacement text are remembered between sessions. After finishing in the current view, Penpoint offers to continue replacing across your whole manuscript. A new swap button flips find and replace values with one click, and pressing Enter in the Replace field searches and replaces in one step.
